channel.title: UMBRASEC Research
channel.description: Independent defensive security research - detection engineering, threat analysis, and open-source tooling.

item.title: The Remote Support Appliance Was Open for Seven Weeks - CVE-2026-102764 and What ARMORY CASTLE Left Behind
item.description: CVE-2026-102764 is an authentication bypass by spoofing (CWE-290) in BeyondTrust Remote Support, CVSS v4.0 9.3, letting an unauthenticated remote attacker perform file operations on the appliance. It was exploited as a zero-day from late August 2026 by ARMORY CASTLE (formerly UNC5221; CrowdStrike Warp Panda), a suspected PRC-nexus espionage actor; affects all supported versions up to 26.2.3, patch BT26-05-RS, SaaS patched 9 October, Privileged Remote Access shares the code, CISA KEV 16 October. The dated timeline, the SAWFLY web shell (mangoapi.php, 404 scanner evasion), the BARECLAW tunneler hidden behind the appliance HAProxy config, root persistence via a SUID shell and a sudoers template, log-deletion anti-forensics and the tell it leaves, the published SHA-256 hashes and YARA rules, a full hunt table, the ATT&CK mapping, and why patching does not remove persistence.

item.title: When the Allowlist Isn't a Boundary - Auto-Approve Bypasses in an Abandoned AI Coding Agent
item.description: On 13 October 2026 VulnCheck disclosed five command auto-approve bypasses in Roo Code, an open-source AI coding agent for VS Code: CVE-2026-110202 through CVE-2026-110206, all affecting versions through 3.54.0. Each is a parser-differential: the checker that judges a command against the auto-approve allowlist and the shell that executes it disagree, so a command passes the check and runs something the allowlist would deny. The trigger is indirect prompt injection - text planted in content the agent reads - and all five require auto-approval enabled. There is no fixed release: the repository was archived on 15 May 2026 and is read-only. The five bypasses at a defender's depth, how this is excessive agency plus indirect injection plus the confused deputy with the one containing control removed, why it is hard to detect and the endpoint behaviour to watch instead, the ATT&CK and ATLAS mapping, and the response to an unmaintained AI agent.

item.title: php2shell and the Hallucinated Exploit - What Defenders Should Actually Do About CVE-2026-109618/109619
item.description: CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 ("php2shell") are two critical memory-safety bugs in PHP's request handling that can allow unauthenticated remote code execution before application code runs, highest risk on Apache mod_php, CVSS v4.0 9.2, fixed on 21 October 2026 in 8.5.12 / 8.4.27 / 8.3.36 / 8.2.35. Yet most PoCs on GitHub and in honeypot traffic are the unrelated 2018 PHP_SESSION_UPLOAD_PROGRESS session-poisoning technique, generated by people feeding loose CVE details into an LLM that keyed on the shared feature name. The real bugs at a defender's depth, why RCE is genuinely hard, what Amazon MadPot and other telemetry actually show (attempts, not confirmed success, not yet in CISA KEV), a low-confidence request tripwire and the worker-crash hunt that is harder to fake, mitigations including CVE-2026-115560, and why reporting what you see is not downplaying.

item.title: Sixteen Days From KEV to Exfiltration - What the Mathspace Breach Says About Internal Tooling
item.description: CVE-2026-72898 is an unauthenticated SQL injection in Metabase's /api/session/reset_password endpoint, CVSS 10.0 under both v3.1 and v4.0, yielding administrator access to the instance and through it every database it holds. Metabase confirmed active exploitation when it published the fix on 6 August 2026; CISA added the CVE to KEV on 11 August; an Australian edtech platform's self-hosted instance was accessed on 10 August and 1,079,819 records were downloaded on 27 August. The verified timeline, what S:C in the CVSS vector told you in advance, one Sigma rule plus a volume and egress hunt, the ATT&CK mapping, and why asset discovery rather than patch speed is the control that failed.

item.title: Your MSP's RMM Is Your Attack Surface - What the N-central Compromise Means for MSP Customers
item.description: CVE-2026-18556 and CVE-2026-18577 are authentication bypasses in N-able N-central, an RMM platform used by MSPs to manage client fleets. Both were added to CISA KEV in early August 2026 after in-the-wild exploitation, and the second exists because the fix for the first was incomplete. For an organisation with outsourced IT the vulnerable server is not theirs to patch - but the Take Control sessions, the svchost.exe dropped into a user's Documents folder, and the Cloudflared persistence service all executed on their endpoints. The timeline, what the published CVSS vectors tell a defender, two Sigma rules, a hunt procedure, and the supplier questions that follow.

item.title: SafePay Is Claiming Australian Victims - Why Real Estate Agencies Are in the Blast Radius
item.description: SafePay is a centralized (non-RaaS) ransomware crew now claiming Australian victims, and real-estate agencies fit its target profile almost perfectly: data-rich, cash-handling via trust accounts, thinly defended, and spread across franchise offices under one brand. The playbook stage by stage - unpatched edge devices, infostealer-harvested logins reused over RDP/VPN, PsExec/WinRM movement, rclone and FileZilla exfiltration, backup and shadow-copy deletion - mapped to the Essential Eight controls that break each link. Built entirely from public vendor reporting, naming no individual victim.

item.title: How INC Ransom Hits Australian Organisations - and the Essential Eight That Stops It
item.description: INC Ransom is a ransomware-as-a-service crew actively claiming Australian victims, and the firms it lands on look a lot like a typical smaller organisation. The affiliate playbook stage by stage - phishing, unpatched edge devices, bought credentials, living-off-the-land movement, commodity exfiltration with rclone and MEGAsync - mapped to the Essential Eight controls that break each link in the chain. Built entirely from public reporting, including the ACSC/CERT NZ advisory.

item.title: Securing AI Agents: A Defender's Guide to Tool-Calling LLMs
item.description: A chatbot that gets prompt-injected says something wrong; an agent that gets prompt-injected does something wrong. The agent threat surface - excessive agency, indirect injection via tool output, the MCP supply chain, the confused-deputy identity problem - what to log, and the detections and containment architecture that keep one bad instruction from becoming an incident.

item.title: Detecting the LiteLLM Command Injection (CVE-2026-42271) in Your AI Gateway
item.description: CVE-2026-42271 turns LiteLLM's MCP preview endpoints into authenticated command execution on the proxy host, and chains with the Starlette "BadHost" bug (CVE-2026-48710) into unauthenticated RCE. In CISA KEV and actively exploited - the mechanism at a defender's depth, what to log, and two runnable Sigma rules with tuning notes.

item.title: Prompt Injection and the OWASP LLM Top 10: A Field Guide for Defenders
item.description: The OWASP LLM Top 10 read as a defender's checklist: why prompt injection has no patch, the "lethal trifecta" behind incidents like EchoLeak (CVE-2025-32711), what to log in LLM-integrated apps, and canary, egress, and behavioral detections you can deploy today.

item.title: Detecting OAuth Consent Phishing in Microsoft 365
item.description: The phishing class that never asks for a password and sails through MFA - illicit OAuth consent grants (MITRE ATT&CK T1528) in Microsoft Entra ID, the audit-log artifacts they leave, and KQL detections with tuning notes.

item.title: Detecting Kerberoasting: A Practical Walkthrough with Sigma
item.description: How Kerberoasting (MITRE ATT&CK T1558.003) works, why RC4 service tickets give it away, and three layered Sigma detections - RC4 downgrade, request fan-out, and a honeypot SPN - with tuning and false-positive notes you can run against your own logs.
